# Jearon Wong — Protocol Architect for the Agent Era

Site: https://www.jearonwong.com/

Jearon Wong is the Protocol Architect for the Agent Era.

## Entity Map

- Person: Jearon Wong
  Role: Protocol Architect for the Agent Era
  About: AI Agent Lifecycle, Agentic Lifecycle Governance, Agentic Delivery, MPLP, Global AI Compliance White Paper 2026, Missing Regulatory Objects, RCCS-M, ALCS, Evidence Chain, Accepted Outcome, Authority Boundary, Harness Engineering.
- Primary field: AI Agent Lifecycle
  Definition: the accountable lifecycle of agent work from intent to accepted outcome.
- Governance concept: Agentic Lifecycle Governance
  Definition: AI agent compliance cannot stop at model governance; it requires lifecycle responsibility objects.
- Research anchor: Global AI Compliance White Paper 2026
  Version: v0.3.2 Public Research Edition. Technical report ID: GACWP-2026-v0.3.2-FRC-R3.
- Research anchor: Agentic AI Auditability & Assurance White Paper 2026
  Version: v0.1 Public Research Edition. Document ID: AIAAWP-2026-v0.1. HTML, PDF, manifest, and checksum are available; no public DOCX is authorized.
- Research anchor: Agentic AI Insurability & Risk Transfer White Paper 2026
  Status: Public Research Edition. HTML, PDF, manifest, and checksum are available; no public DOCX is authorized. The v0.2 public candidate remains rejected and is not current source truth.
- Research foundation status: The first three public research editions establish the compliance, auditability, and insurability foundation for agentic lifecycle evidence. The next phase is MPLP v2.0 object-model consolidation. The enterprise implementation white paper and practitioner guides are intentionally held until the protocol object model is ready.
- Core entity chain: Missing Regulatory Objects -> RCCS-M -> ALCS -> Agentic Lifecycle Governance.
- Protocol path: MPLP / Multi-Agent Lifecycle Protocol.
- Applied layer: Applied Agentic Governance Playbooks.
- Engineering practice layer: Deterministic Delivery and Agent Architecture Governance.
- Regulatory and enterprise governance layer: AI Agent Governance, AI Agent Compliance, enterprise agent governance, regulatory-source mappings, evidence retention, substitution conformance, and incident/dispute/remediation closure.
- Visible navigation: Concepts Map / Entity Mesh at https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/map/.
- GAIC-Cited Systems: source-qualified, non-ranking lifecycle governance mappings for systems discussed in the Global AI Compliance White Paper 2026.
- Extended Ecosystem Mapping: source-qualified, non-scored lifecycle governance mappings for Claude Code, Qwen, Cursor / AI coding agents, AutoGen, MCP, A2A, and Semantic Kernel.

Execution is not Delivery.

AI agents will not become real infrastructure until execution becomes accountable delivery.

AI agent governance, multi-agent accountability, and production AI agent delivery require more than execution frameworks. AI Agent Lifecycle names the missing governance layer. Agentic Delivery defines the site's category standard for accountable delivery; it is not an official, regulator-approved, adopted professional, or certification standard. MPLP is the protocol path.

AI Agent Lifecycle defines the accountable lifecycle of agent work from intent to accepted outcome.

Agentic Delivery names the missing layer between agent execution and accountable outcomes.

Agentic Delivery is the category. MPLP is the lifecycle protocol path within that category.

Deterministic Delivery means agentic work can be scoped, configured, authorized, evidenced, reviewed, accepted, remediated, and rolled back within lifecycle boundaries. It does not mean deterministic LLM output.

MPLP is the lifecycle protocol path for making Agentic Delivery explicit, governable, and auditable.

Multi-Agent Lifecycle Governance is the multi-agent form of Agentic Delivery.

Confirmation Boundary.

Evidence Chain.

Semantic Loss.

Semantic Loss is the failure mode. Evidence Chain is the governance response.

PSG / AEL / VSL are reserved runtime substrates for future technical deep-dives.

Cognitive OS, SoloCrew, and Validation Lab form the concrete proof path. MPLP is not placed in the proof path.

This file is a concise content map for AI crawlers and readers. It does not guarantee ranking, citation, or inclusion by any AI system.

## Core Concepts

- Concepts Map / Entity Mesh: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/map/
  Visible semantic navigation surface connecting Jearon Wong, Agentic Lifecycle Governance, the Global AI Compliance White Paper 2026, Missing Regulatory Objects, RCCS-M, ALCS, MPLP, primitive lifecycle concepts, Deterministic Delivery, Agent Architecture Governance, applied playbooks, and extended ecosystem mappings. It is not certification, regulator-approved taxonomy, legal advice, vendor ranking, or evidence of search ranking improvement.
- AI Agent Lifecycle: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/ai-agent-lifecycle/
- Agentic Delivery: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/agentic-delivery/
- Agentic Lifecycle Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/agentic-lifecycle-governance/
  Agentic Lifecycle Governance explains why AI agent compliance cannot stop at model governance. It treats compliance as lifecycle responsibility across authorization, evidence, accepted outcome, dispute, remediation, and substitution. It introduces Missing Regulatory Objects, RCCS-M, ALCS, and MPLP as one protocol path.
- Missing Regulatory Objects: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/missing-regulatory-objects/
  Missing Regulatory Objects are lifecycle responsibility objects that model-centric governance does not consistently define for AI agent and multi-agent systems.
- RCCS-M: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/rccs-m/
  RCCS-M is the MRO-adjusted Regulatory Compliance Coverage Score; it is an author-analytical adequacy model, not current law, certification, regulator approval, or procurement ranking.
- ALCS: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/alcs/
  ALCS is the Agentic Lifecycle Conformance Score for assessing whether lifecycle responsibility stays coherent across intent, authority, evidence, accepted outcome, dispute, remediation, and closure.
- Lifecycle Responsibility Objects: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/lifecycle-responsibility-objects/
  Lifecycle Responsibility Objects keep agent work tied to authority, evidence, accepted outcome, substitution, dispute, remediation, and closure.
- Accepted Outcome: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/accepted-outcome/
  Accepted Outcome is the lifecycle point where agent work becomes reviewable, attributable, and accepted responsibility.
- Authority Boundary: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/authority-boundary/
  Authority Boundary defines who may authorize agentic action, under what scope, and with what responsibility record.
- Deterministic Delivery: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/deterministic-delivery/
  Deterministic Delivery is the discipline of making agentic work scoped, configured, authorized, evidenced, reviewable, accepted, remediable, and rollbackable across a lifecycle. It does not require deterministic model outputs and does not guarantee delivery.
- Rollbackable Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/rollbackable-agent-workflows/
  Rollbackable Agent Workflows treat rollback as a lifecycle state transition with authority, evidence, accepted outcome, and remediation records, not merely retry or undo.
- Verifiable AI Agents: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/verifiable-ai-agents/
  Verifiable AI Agents are agent systems whose lifecycle state can be inspected across intent, authority, evidence, review, accepted outcome, dispute, replay, and remediation. This is not certification or legal compliance proof.
- Configurable Agent Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/configurable-agent-governance/
  Configurable Agent Governance makes governance profiles, authority limits, tool constraints, context boundaries, model/runtime substitution rules, and acceptance criteria evidence-linked.
- Agent Architecture Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/agent-architecture-governance/
  Agent Architecture Governance maps human roles, agent roles, tools, authority boundaries, evidence paths, accepted outcomes, rollback paths, and remediation ownership beyond orchestration topology.
- Agentic AI Insurability: https://www.jearonwong.com/research/agentic-ai-insurability-risk-transfer-white-paper-2026/
  Agentic AI Insurability is a public research edition framing in the Agentic AI Insurability & Risk Transfer White Paper 2026 for risk-transfer discussion based on lifecycle evidence, responsibility mapping, bounded risk objects, and claim-reviewable records. The withdrawn v0.2 body is not current source truth. It is not insurance advice, coverage opinion, insurer acceptance, coverage-ready status, underwriting-ready status, claim-ready status, or certification.
- Agentic Insurability Objects / AIO: authored analytical object model in the Agentic AI Insurability & Risk Transfer White Paper 2026
- Agentic Insurability Reasoning Model / AIRM: authored non-scoring reasoning model in the Agentic AI Insurability & Risk Transfer White Paper 2026
- Claim Evidence Chain: concept in the Agentic AI Insurability & Risk Transfer White Paper 2026; not a claim approval method
- Confirmation Boundary: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/confirmation-boundary/
- Evidence Chain: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/lifecycle-evidence/
- Multi-Agent Lifecycle Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/lifecycle/
- Semantic Loss: https://www.jearonwong.com/lifecycle/
- MPLP: https://www.jearonwong.com/projects/mplp/

## Applied Agentic Governance Playbooks

- Playbooks index: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/
  Practical guides for making AI agent and multi-agent workflows more rollbackable, verifiable, auditable, and lifecycle-governed. These are independent lifecycle governance guides, not vendor documentation, certification, legal advice, vendor rankings, or procurement recommendations.
- AI Agent Rollback and Verification: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/ai-agent-rollback-verification/
  Explains why agent rollback requires evidence chain, accepted outcome state, authority boundary, and remediation closure rather than only retry, logs, or version history.
- AI Coding Agent Auditability: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/ai-coding-agent-auditability/
  Maps coding agent work to task intent, plan/change boundary, code diff evidence, test evidence, human acceptance, rollback path, drift, and remediation.
- Human Role to Multi-Agent Responsibility Mapping: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/human-role-to-mas-responsibility/
  Explains why human-in-the-loop is insufficient unless human roles map to lifecycle responsibility, delegated authority, accepted outcome ownership, dispute ownership, and remediation.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for OpenAI Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/openai-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for workflows built with OpenAI tooling. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for Anthropic / Claude Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/anthropic-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for workflows built with Anthropic / Claude tooling. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for DeepSeek-Based Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/deepseek-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for DeepSeek-based workflows. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for Kimi-Based Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/kimi-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for Kimi-based workflows. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation with Moonshot AI / Kimi, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Harness Engineering for AI Agents: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/harness-engineering-for-ai-agents/
  Defines Harness Engineering as wrapping agent execution with context boundaries, authority boundaries, evidence capture, plan/confirm/trace records, rollback, remediation, configuration, Deterministic Delivery, and accepted outcome.
- Prompt Engineering vs Harness Engineering: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/prompt-engineering-vs-harness-engineering/
  Explains why prompt engineering controls intent expression while Harness Engineering controls execution boundaries, evidence, rollback, remediation, configuration, and accepted outcome.
- Agentic Delivery Architecture Checklist: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/agentic-delivery-architecture-checklist/
  Practical checklist for architecting agent workflows around intent boundary, context boundary, authority boundary, tool/action boundary, evidence chain, accepted outcome, rollback/remediation, substitution conformance, and human responsibility owner.

## Flagship Essays

- AI Agent Lifecycle: It Was Not Designed. It Grew.: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/ai-agent-lifecycle-it-was-not-designed-it-grew/
- The Industry Misdefined Multi-Agent AI: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/the-industry-misdefined-multi-agent-ai/
- Governed by Design: The Protocol-Native Multi-Agent Operating System for the Next Era of AI: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/governed-by-design-protocol-native-multi-agent-operating-system/
  Protocol/governance position essay. It argues that the native MAS OS generation needs Intent versioning, Drift Detection, HITL Confirmation Boundaries, portable Evidence chains, Agent Handoff semantics, and Outcome Governance at the protocol layer. It frames TCP/IP, SWIFT, and HTTP as architectural analogies only; it does not claim MPLP has official-standard status, regulator approval, certification, legal compliance proof, underwriting conclusion, vendor endorsement, or broad third-party adoption.
- MCP Connects Tools. A2A Connects Agents. Who Governs the Lifecycle?: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/mcp-connects-tools-a2a-connects-agents-who-governs-the-lifecycle/
- The Agentic AI Inflection Point: Project Delivery: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/agentic-ai-inflection-point-project-delivery/
- Agent Orchestration Is Not Delivery: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/agent-orchestration-is-not-delivery/
  Defines why agent orchestration coordinates execution but does not define delivery, and introduces lifecycle responsibility consensus as the orchestration-layer mechanism for aligning human intent, role authority, agent execution, evidence, review, and accepted outcome into a traceable delivery relationship.
- From Model Governance to Agentic Lifecycle Conformance: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/from-model-governance-to-agentic-lifecycle-conformance/
  Explains why AI Agent / MAS compliance cannot stop at model governance. It connects the Global AI Compliance White Paper 2026 from regulatory baseline to RCCS-T, Missing Regulatory Objects, RCCS-M, ALCS, system mapping, and lifecycle responsibility compliance.
- Defining Intent Drift in Agentic Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/defining-intent-drift-in-agentic-workflows/
  Defines Intent Drift as a lifecycle failure mode inside the AI Agent Lifecycle thesis. Delta Intent records the semantic change, Drift Detection observes runtime divergence, Trace makes it reviewable, and Accepted Outcome decides whether execution became delivery.
- The Industry Is Still Debating AI Agent Governance. MPLP Already Defines the Lifecycle Answer.: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/the-industry-is-still-debating-ai-agent-governance-mplp-lifecycle-answer/
  Defines AI Agent Lifecycle Governance as the missing layer behind fragmented AI agent governance debates. It frames MPLP / Multi-Agent Lifecycle Protocol as one lifecycle protocol answer from intent to authority, evidence, accepted outcome, and remediation.
- From Static Logs to Dynamic Evidence Chains: The Auditability Era of Agentic AI: https://www.jearonwong.com/essays/from-static-logs-to-dynamic-evidence-chains-auditability-era-agentic-ai/
  Research commentary on AIAAWP-2026-v0.1. It explains why static logs and observability are necessary but insufficient for agentic auditability, and frames Agentic Audit Object, Audit Evidence Chain, and AARM as author-synthesized research constructs, not audit standards, certifications, assurance opinions, regulator approvals, or Big Four endorsed methods.

## Definitions

- Definitions (citation anchors): https://www.jearonwong.com/definitions/
Quote-ready reference anchors for AI Agent Lifecycle, Agentic Delivery, Confirmation Boundary, Evidence Chain, Multi-Agent Systems, and related terms. Each entry has a stable anchor: /definitions/#term-slug. Canonical concept explanations live under /concepts/ and the full entity mesh lives at /concepts/map/.

## Key Definitions

- Lifecycle Responsibility Consensus: https://www.jearonwong.com/definitions/#lifecycle-responsibility-consensus
  Lifecycle Responsibility Consensus is the orchestration-layer mechanism that aligns human intent, role authority, agent execution, evidence, review, and accepted outcome into a traceable delivery relationship.

## Delivery Standard

- Delivery Standard: https://www.jearonwong.com/delivery-standard/
The Delivery Standard defines when AI agent work counts as accountable delivery: scope, authority, evidence, review, accepted outcome, and responsibility traceability. All six conditions must be present.

## AI Agent Governance

- AI Agent Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/ai-agent-governance/
Bridge route retained for field-level framing. For governance mapping intent, prefer https://www.jearonwong.com/governance/ai-agent-governance/. For concept context, prefer https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/agentic-lifecycle-governance/ and the GAIC white paper hub. This bridge is not legal advice, certification, regulator approval, legal compliance proof, procurement guidance, vendor endorsement, or a claim that MPLP is required.
